item.title: Danish FA chief says FIFA Legal Committee evaded questions on Infantino proposal
item.description: Denmark's football chief said on Saturday that FIFA declined to answer "critical questions" at a Legal Committee meeting about its abandoned proposal to sell commercial stakes in tournaments as he renewed calls for President Gianni Infantino to step down.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Denmark's football chief said on Saturday that FIFA declined to answer "critical questions" at a Legal Committee meeting about its abandoned proposal to sell commercial stakes in tournaments as he renewed calls for President Gianni Infantino to step down. Danish FA (DBU) President Jesper Moller said he was surprised that the [USN:L1N43X04P TEXT:"now-abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise"] was not on the agenda and was frustrated by the world soccer governing body's evasive response to his inquiries. "I naturally used the meeting to ask a number of critical questions about the process, which I still consider to have been deeply problematic," Moller said in a statement. "I am surprised that FIFA Forward Enterprise has not been discussed by the Legal Committee, which is precisely the body that should be consulted on legal matters concerning FIFA. "But unfortunately, it proved impossible to get answers to the questions, as FIFA wants to await the discussion at the upcoming Council meeting in October. "This would clearly have been a good opportunity for FIFA's leadership to explain itself." Reuters has contacted FIFA for comment. The FIFA Council comprises 37 members including president Infantino, eight vice-presidents and 28 other members elected by the member associations. "We will continue to push for answers and I am confident that we will get to the bottom of this completely unacceptable matter," Moller added. "The meeting confirmed that FIFA cannot rebuild its credibility under the current leadership. The time has come for a change of president at FIFA." 'CREDIBLE ALTERNATIVE' TO INFANTINO Last month, the [USN:L4N44I0QX TEXT:"DBU vowed to find a credible alternative"] to Infantino in next year's election, saying it had lost confidence in the Swiss-Italian after his aborted proposal to sell commercial stakes in FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup. "I will continue working closely with my European colleagues to find a candidate who can command a majority. There is no trust in Infantino and FIFA's leadership," Moller said. FIFA had apologised to member associations for mistakes made over the abandoned proposal, but its leadership reaffirmed support for Infantino after a crisis meeting in Morocco. The DBU said Infantino's proposal had created "a fundamental crisis of confidence in FIFA's leadership" that could not be repaired by withdrawals or apologies. However, [USN:L6N4520VY TEXT:"Infantino can count on enough votes"] to win re-election, meaning his opponents will need to shift strategy and focus on curbing his powers, multiple sources familiar with the discussions told Reuters. The FIFA presidential election will take place in Rabat on March 18, 2027. Infantino's plan prompted a global backlash, with UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and North America's CONCACAF among those calling for change at the top of FIFA while the possibility of a [USN:L6N44G0N5 TEXT:"no-confidence vote"] was also discussed. Several European national associations have since withdrawn backing for Infantino's re-election, including the [USN:L6N4510X8 TEXT:"French Football Federation"] on Thursday, while Austria's FA (OFB) also withdrew support. "The Supervisory Board of the OFB unanimously decided not to support Gianni Infantino's renewed candidacy as FIFA President," it said in a statement. "The basis for this decision is the developments of recent weeks and months and the resulting significant changes in the framework conditions."

item.title: GB-Reform UK a reçu deux dons de €42 mlns de crypto-milliardaires en 48 heures
item.description: Reform UK a reçu un deuxième don de 36 millions de livres sterling (42 millions d'euros) en l'espace de 48 heures, a annoncé samedi son auteur, alors que le parti populiste anti-immigration de Nigel Farage vise la victoire aux élections législatives prévues d'ici à la mi-2029.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Reform UK a reçu un deuxième don de 36 millions de livres sterling (42 millions d'euros) en l'espace de 48 heures, a annoncé samedi son auteur, alors que le parti populiste anti-immigration de Nigel Farage vise la victoire aux élections législatives prévues d'ici à la mi-2029. Le milliardaire des cryptomonnaies Christopher Harborne, déjà le plus grand donateur de Reform UK, annonce dans les colonnes du journal The Telegraph qu'il a fait un don similaire à celui d'un autre crypto-milliardaire, Ben Delo, qui avait été condamné en 2022 aux États-Unis pour violation de la loi sur le secret bancaire avant d'être gracié par Donald Trump. "Un pays fort est un pays qui s'appuie sur une économie dynamique, créatrice d'emplois. C'est pourquoi j'investis mon argent dans ce que je considère comme la seule cause viable capable de mener à bien la relance", écrit Christopher Harborne, qui a déjà donné près de 100 millions de livres à Reform UK. "Je pense que Nigel Farage et son parti comprennent parfaitement ce qu'un gouvernement doit faire pour remettre notre pays sur la bonne voie. "Alors que je versais chaque mois environ 1 million de livres sterling à Reform, Ben Delo m'a annoncé qu'il allait faire un don record de 36 millions de livres sterling. Mon esprit de compétition m'a poussé à égaler ce montant, et c'est ce que j'ai fait", ajoute l'investisseur. Nigel Farage a promis de transformer son pays en "Hub crypto" s'il parvient au pouvoir. Les donations individuelles aux partis politiques ne sont pas plafonnées au Royaume-uni, comme c'est le cas en France par exemple, à condition que le donateur soit domicilié sur le sol britannique, ce qui est le cas des deux milliardaires, Ben Delo ayant récemment rapatrié son domicile fiscal de Hong Kong à la Grande-Bretagne.

item.title: Cricket Root takes charge, guiding England to series whitewash over Pakistan
item.description: Joe Root guided England to a 3-0 series whitewash over Pakistan with an unbeaten 62, as his side overcame early tremors to win the third test by eight wickets at Edgbaston.
item.dc:creator: Neil Squires
item.content:encoded: Joe Root guided England to a 3-0 series whitewash over Pakistan with an unbeaten 62, as his side overcame early tremors to win the third test by eight wickets at Edgbaston. England, chasing a victory target of 130, lost Ben Duckett to the first ball and opening partner Emilio Gay later in the same over from Muhammad Abbas. But Root, who had a fortunate escape when he was bowled by Mohammad Ali on 23 off a no ball, brought all his experience to bear as England wrapped up their first series win for 19 months. It was Ali’s 17th no ball of the series. Pakistan’s last chance came and went when Root, on 38, edged Abbas between first and second slip who both left the ball for each other. It was Root’s 110th innings of 50 or more in test cricket, a total which includes 41 hundreds. Pakistan, who conceded a first innings deficit of 320, showed commendable fight to take the game into a fourth day, but with Jordan Cox supplying solid back-up to his captain with an unbeaten 59, England eased to victory in the 25th over. If only Pakistan had shown up in the first two tests as they did belatedly in Birmingham this could have been an enthralling series. As it was, England's total dominance made it something of a damp squib. England, attempting to reboot after the New Zealand defeat which followed the Ashes loss, will not be complaining. Notwithstanding the panic induced by Pakistan’s exciting debutant Razaullah, whose thrilling 81 from 63 balls electrified Edgbaston on Friday evening, it has been a satisfying return to the captaincy for Root following Ben Stokes’ retirement from international cricket. Marcus Trescothick, appointed interim red-ball head coach after the sacking of Brendon McCullum, hands over a rejuvenated side to Stephen Fleming for the three-test series in South Africa in December and January. South Africa will be much stronger opposition, but if England can keep the quartet of Ollie Robinson, Jofra Archer, Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson fit, they will be a threat. The England pace bowling attack, led by Robinson who took 21 wickets, was too good for Pakistan on helpful surfaces. The batting was not quite so convincing with no one able to make a century. With Jacob Bethell due to come back in for the winter tour after knee surgery, one batsman out of Emilio Gay, Dan Lawrence and Cox will have to make way. That situation remains fluid but Cox, who also kept wicket in the second innings because of Jamie Smith’s finger injury, did his cause no harm with his poised second innings performance. For Pakistan, who have now lost 16 of their 21 tests, it has been a chaotic tour capped off by the decision to replace seven players in the squad after the second test and sack coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and his assistant Umar Gul. At least, though, the ‘Raz-ball’ fightback in Birmingham showed there was still a pulse ahead of their next assignment against Sri Lanka in October.

item.title: Japan and Fiji through to Pacific Nations Cup final
item.description: Hosts Japan will take on defending champions Fiji in next weekend’s Pacific Nations Championship final after both sides scored convincing semi-final wins in Higashiosaka on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hosts Japan will take on defending champions Fiji in next weekend’s Pacific Nations Championship final after both sides scored convincing semi-final wins in Higashiosaka on Saturday. Record seven-times champions Fiji scored their first try after 20 seconds and went on to a 45-29 victory over Canada followed by Japan's 63-14 triumph over the United States. Fiji’s seven-try blitz started inside the first minute when Kitione Salawa charged down a clearance to go over, although Canada spilt several chances to reduce the islanders’ margin of victory. Japan romped to a 28-0 lead after 15 minutes and finished with nine converted tries in a one-sided showing. The final will be in Tokyo next Saturday when Fiji will aim to beat Japan to the title for the third straight year.

item.title: Walbert Urena eyes 10th win as Angels take on Nationals
item.description: Rookie right-hander Walbert Urena, one of the few bright spots in an otherwise forgettable season for the Los Angeles Angels, will try to pick up his 10th win when the Angels visit the Washington Nationals on Saturday afternoon in the second game of their three-game series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Rookie right-hander Walbert Urena, one of the few bright spots in an otherwise forgettable season for the Los Angeles Angels, will try to pick up his 10th win when the Angels visit the Washington Nationals on Saturday afternoon in the second game of their three-game series. Urena (9-10, 2.74 ERA), who has never faced Washington, has a glossy 2.26 ERA to go with a 4-4 record over his last 11 starts. He was a hard-luck 1-0 loser in his most recent start on Sunday at Pittsburgh when he threw his first career complete game, allowing one run -- a third-inning homer down the left-field line to Henry Davis -- and three hits over eight innings while walking one and striking out four. The 22-year-old throws a power sinker that often tops 100 mph. He also throws a changeup in the low 90s, a sweeper, and a four-seam fastball that hit 101.1 mph against the Pirates. "He's strong, man," Los Angeles manager Kurt Suzuki said. "We've seen it all year. It's 100 pitches, and he's still throwing 100 and it looks pretty effortless. ... The sky's the limit for him. He just keeps getting better and better." Left-hander Andrew Alvarez (2-6, 3.60 ERA), an Anaheim, Calif., native who went to nearby Los Alamitos High School, will face his hometown team for the first time. Alvarez comes in off his team's 7-5 loss to the Los Angeles Dodgers on Sunday at Dodger Stadium, allowing three runs on four hits over 4 1/3 innings, with two walks and five strikeouts. Washington (68-81) scored three runs in the eighth inning to rally for a 4-3 victory over the Angels (56-91) in Friday night's series opener, snapping a seven-game losing streak. Jorbit Vivas hit a two-run, go-ahead double, and CJ Abrams had a double and two hits and a run to lead the Nationals on offense. Starter Cade Cavalli gave up two runs on three hits over six-plus innings and struck out nine but didn't figure into the decision. Erik Tolman picked up his second save -- barely -- allowing one run on one hit and a walk in the ninth. Trailing 4-2 heading into the ninth, the Angels nearly tied the score when Christian Moore drilled a two-out double to right-center that bounced off the top of the fence, driving in Oswald Peraza, who had walked. Tolman then got pinch hitter Kyren Paris on a lazy fly ball to left to end the game. It marked just the second time in 63 games that Washington won when trailing after seven innings. "You've got to be able to win games in different ways," manager Blake Butera said. "And I think we did a good job of that tonight, playing really good baseball. It's nice to win that one." Angels outfielder Mike Trout hit his 21st home run of the season in the first inning, a 416-foot drive to left-center. It was the 425th homer of his career and snapped a 27-game homerless drought. "It's good to see one go out, obviously," Trout said. "I've been battling stuff since the (All-Star) break. But yeah, it's good to see one go out." --Field Level Media

item.title: Guardians riding boost of energy into rematch vs. Twins
item.description: Travis Bazzana knows how calendars work.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Travis Bazzana knows how calendars work. This month is September. Next month is October. Every game is more exciting than the last. Bazzana and his teammates will look to deliver another victory when the Cleveland Guardians (75-73) play the Minnesota Twins (69-78) on Saturday afternoon in Minneapolis. Cleveland is coming off a 5-2 win in Friday's series opener. The Guardians pulled within a half-game of the slumping Chicago White Sox (75-72) for first place in the American League Central. Moreover, Cleveland is two games ahead of Toronto in the race for the third AL wild-card spot. "I mean, I'm looking at the (playoff) race, and it fires me up every day," Bazzana said. "You know, it gives you that extra little fire for the day when you know you've got to win and you're a step closer to winning the division. "It doesn't make me nervous. ... I feel really good about where I'm at right now, and I'm just enjoying every day. But I think it gives us a good feeling and an extra boost of energy to go get it done in September." Cleveland is trying to win the division and reach the playoffs for the third year in a row. The franchise has played in the postseason seven times in the past 10 seasons. One reason for the Guardians' success as of late is Brayan Rocchio, who came through again Friday with a two-run double in the top of the ninth inning. Cleveland manager Stephen Vogt said Rocchio loves playing in the spotlight. "It's September and it's 'Rocchy,'" Vogt said. "We always feel good when he's at the plate, regardless of the time of year. But he steps up big for this team. "That's another really good at-bat (on Friday). You know, (he) took a shot early and then really shortened up and took what the pitcher gave him." Twins left-hander Connor Prielipp (4-7, 5.25 ERA) will try to cool down Rocchio and the rest of the Guardians. Prielipp is set to make the 20th start of his rookie campaign. In his most recent start, Prielipp drew a no-decision after allowing two runs on five hits in four innings against the Detroit Tigers. He walked none and struck out five. Prielipp has faced the Guardians twice. He is 0-1 with a 3.60 ERA in those games. Cleveland will counter with right-hander Daniel Espino (0-0, 2.70). He also is a rookie, and he will make his first start after appearing in nine games out of the bullpen. The 25-year-old from Panama has struck out 18 batters in 10 innings this season. He has never faced the Twins in his career. Minnesota will play without All-Star outfielder Byron Buxton. The team announced Friday that he is scheduled to undergo season-ending surgery on his injured hip. Buxton hit .254 this season with 25 homers and 46 RBIs in 93 games. "He's a grinder," Twins catcher Ryan Jeffers said. "He's been fighting through this for a little while, and he's done some unbelievable things this year. We all know the player he is, the person he is. "Yeah, it puts a damper on the excellent season he had this year, but it doesn't put a damper on the impact he's had in this clubhouse and on the young guys." --Field Level Media

item.title: BRICS adopts joint declaration, urges 'maximum restraint' in Mideast
item.description: The BRICS group of nations unanimously adopted a joint declaration on Saturday, expressing "deep concern" over the war in the Middle East and urged maximum restraint, advocating for a "multilateral approach" that respects national viewpoints.
item.dc:creator: Sarita Singh
item.content:encoded: The BRICS group of nations [USN:L6N45402F TEXT:"unanimously adopted"] a joint declaration on Saturday, expressing "deep concern" over the war in the Middle East and urged maximum restraint, advocating for a "multilateral approach" that respects national viewpoints. The declaration, adopted on the first day of the BRICS leaders' annual summit in New Delhi, comes at a time when U.S. and Iran have resumed tit-for-tat strikes against each other, after a pause in fighting for much of August. The [USN:L6N4510UT TEXT:"BRICS bloc"] includes both Iran and Washington-ally United Arab Emirates, which was expected to make clinching a joint statement consensus a particularly challenging task for host New Delhi. "We express deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in Middle East...call for exercising maximum restraint...avoiding actions that could further aggravate the situation," the 'New Delhi Declaration' said. The declaration also reiterated the commitment of member nations to a peaceful resolution of international disputes "through dialogue, consultation, and diplomacy". In addition, they voiced concerns about the rise of "unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures" that distort trade, against the backdrop of U.S. sanctions against Tehran [USN:L6N4530LJ TEXT:"amid its war"] with the country, and against Russia over its conflict with Ukraine. BRICS includes Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates.

item.title: Padres turn to Michael King as they scrap with Giants amid tight NL wild-card race
item.description: The San Diego Padres will have the advantage of playing while the rival Arizona Diamondbacks watch from afar when the Padres continue a road series against the San Francisco Giants on Saturday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The San Diego Padres will have the advantage of playing while the rival Arizona Diamondbacks watch from afar when the Padres continue a road series against the San Francisco Giants on Saturday afternoon. Moments after San Francisco's Oracle Park scoreboard flashed an Arizona win over the Texas Rangers in Phoenix on Friday night -- a victory that temporarily moved the Diamondbacks (79-69) into a tie for the final National League wild-card spot -- the Padres survived a tense finish with the Giants to move back in front in the race with a 7-5 victory to improve to 79-68. Down 7-1 at one point, San Francisco pulled to 7-5, then loaded the bases against San Diego closer Mason Miller with two outs in the ninth. Miller then struck out one of the Giants' hottest hitters, Bryce Eldridge, to allow the Padres to breathe a sigh of relief. Jackson Merrill, who contributed three hits and two runs to the Padres' fifth straight win, told a national television audience afterward that his club is doing a good job of focusing on the task at hand. "Every game is a new day. Come out ready to compete and try to win a baseball game, not focus a lot on the race or anything," he said. "Try to get to the end of the season with as many wins as possible under our belt." With a chance to extend their lead to a full game before the Diamondbacks take the field on Saturday night, the Padres have scheduled right-hander Michael King (10-9, 3.00 ERA) to start the rematch vs. the Giants. King will face the Giants for the first time this season but has a history of success over San Francisco, going 3-1 with a 2.22 ERA in five games (four starts) overall and 1-0 with seven innings of shutout ball at Oracle Park. The Giants (62-86) will counter with left-hander Cesar Perdomo (0-0, 0.90 ERA), who will make his home debut. The 24-year-old got a hard-luck no-decision in his first big-league start last Sunday in New York against the Mets, blanking the hosts over six innings in his team's 4-2 loss. Perdomo has never faced the Padres. The Giants' series-opening loss on Friday, which snapped the team's three-game winning streak, featured a grand slam by Rafael Devers and a double, single and RBI by Eldridge before his game-ending strikeout. Jonah Cox, whose bunt single with two outs in the ninth helped get Eldridge to the plate with a chance to be a hero, already recognizes that Eldridge, 21, is going to make the home fans happy more times than not, as he did with a walk-off grand slam in a similar bottom-of-the-ninth situation earlier this season. "People (are) kind of realizing the caliber of player that he is, and I think he's starting to realize it as well," Cox told reporters earlier this week. "He's that guy. He is the guy that we want up in those situations, and it's just really cool to see." Eldridge has never faced King. - Field Level Media

item.title: India's HDFC Bank submits two candidates to RBI for next CEO
item.description: HDFC Bank's board has submitted two candidates to the Reserve Bank of India for the role of CEO, the lender said on Saturday, formally starting the succession process for Sashidhar Jagdishan, who is due to retire later this year.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: HDFC Bank's board has submitted two candidates to the Reserve Bank of India for the role of CEO, the lender said on Saturday, formally starting the succession process for Sashidhar Jagdishan, who is due to retire later this year. The bank did not disclose the names of the candidates. Indian banking rules require private-sector banks to obtain prior RBI approval for the appointment of their managing director and CEO, giving the regulator a key role in vetting senior management. Jagdishan, who has led the bank since 2020, is set to step down at the end of his second term in October. The bank also moved to bolster its board, reappointing V. Srinivasa Rangan as a whole-time director, a regulatory designation for full-time bank directors, and appointing Chief Credit Officer Jimmy Tata to the board in the same capacity. Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha is already a whole-time director. The bank also said it would create a fourth whole-time director position, to be held by the incoming CEO once appointed.

item.title: Farage's Reform UK receives second £36 million pound donation from crypto investor
item.description: Britain's Reform UK has received a £36 million ($48.66 million)donation from cryptocurrency billionaire Christopher Harborne, giving Nigel Farage's party its second huge contribution in the space of two days as it gears up for the next general election.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's Reform UK has received a £36 million ($48.66 million)donation from cryptocurrency billionaire Christopher Harborne, giving Nigel Farage's party its second huge contribution in the space of two days as it gears up for the next general election. Harborne, Reform's biggest donor, said in an article published by the Telegraph newspaper on Saturday that he had matched a record [USN:L1N4530UY TEXT:"£36 million donation"] announced on Friday by fellow cryptocurrency entrepreneur Ben Delo. "A strong country is one that is funded by a vigorous economy which is creating jobs. That’s why I’m putting my money into what I believe is the only viable cause which will get the job of regeneration done," Harborne wrote in the newspaper. "My view is that Nigel Farage and the party fully understand what a government needs to do to get our country back on the right track. "Whilst I have been making donations to Reform of around £1m a month, Ben Delo told me he was going to make a record donation of £36 million. My competitive spirit inspired me to match it, so that is what I’ve done," Harbone said. The donations amount to £72 million in funding for the party over 48 hours. ($1 = 0.7398 pounds)

item.title: Kyle Tucker, Dodgers eager to add to Marlins' misery
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers star Kyle Tucker may be getting hot just in time for the playoffs.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Los Angeles Dodgers star Kyle Tucker may be getting hot just in time for the playoffs. The National League West-leading Dodgers (90-57) will look to extend their winning streak to nine games when they visit the Miami Marlins (72-76) on Saturday. The Marlins, in turn, have lost seven of their past eight games. Tucker went 3-for-3 with a season-high five RBIs in Los Angeles' 6-2 victory over Miami on Friday. He fell a double short of the cycle. Entering Friday, Tucker was on pace for his fourth straight month with an OPS at or below .700, and that's not what the Dodgers thought they were getting when they signed him to a four-year, $240 million contract in January. Tucker, who has posted OPS numbers of .993 and .841 over the past two years, impressed Marlins manager Clayton McCullough with his performance on Friday. "Independent of how this season has gone, (Tucker) is still a terrific hitter," McCullough said. "He handles lefties well. He got a hanging breaking ball and turned the game for them." Tucker produced five straight seasons with more than 20 homers before mustering just 14 in 2026. But if he can finish strong, that will help a Dodgers squad that is missing injured sluggers Shohei Ohtani (right biceps inflammation), Freddie Freeman (right knee) and Andy Pages (left hand). Those three players have hit a combined 67 homers this season. Los Angeles also saw Josue De Paula make his MLB debut on Friday. De Paula went 0-for-3 with a walk after tearing up Double-A pitching. "We want to get him some major-league at-bats to see what it looks like," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. The Dodgers will turn to right-hander Tyler Glasnow (4-0, 3.12 ERA) to make the start on Saturday. His per-nine-innings averages are outstanding in terms of hits allowed (5.3), walks (2.7) and strikeouts (10.9). The Dodgers are 8-2 when he starts, and this will be his fourth start since coming back from a near-three-month injury absence. Glasnow is 1-1 with a 3.86 ERA in five career starts versus the Marlins. Miami will counter with right-hander Tyler Phillips (5-6, 3.51), who is 1-0 with a 6.94 ERA in six career appearances (one start) against the Dodgers. For his career overall, Phillips has a sterling 2.49 ERA in 71 relief appearances, but a 5.13 ERA in 25 career starts. As for Miami's offense, the Marlins are hoping that shortstop Otto Lopez is back on track after a 4-for-5 performance on Friday. This year, Lopez hit .322 in March/April; .339 in May; and .340 in June. That hot start made him a first-time All-Star. However, he batted .284 in July and just .236 in August. Thanks to Friday's big game, he is now hitting .342 in September. "After the phenomenal first half, he struggled for a bit," McCullough said. "He looks to be back in a good spot, hitting the ball to all fields. It's something we have grown accustomed to, and it bodes well for us to have him get hits in bunches." --Field Level Media
